bbc-6-musics-rave-forever.about: A wall-to-wall celebration of dance music from across the decades.

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 19 Jan. Dubbed Berlin’s Queen of House, German DJ and producer Cinthie takes you on a time-travelling night out to 1997, the year her career behind the decks began. Join this celebrated selector as she flexes her extensive record knowledge with a set of wall-to-wall house deep cuts. Expect to hear tracks from R.I.P. Productions, Paul French, Bass Junction and plenty more. A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.
items.title: A Night Out With…Cinthie

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 12 Jan. Cruise through the history of GTA's iconic gaming soundtrack, from past to present. Across three decades, GTA Radio's iconic stations have become a definitive time capsule of club culture, curated by some global heavyweights like The Blessed Madonna, Soulwax, Solomun, and Gilles Peterson. Dial into the sounds of Jaydee, Ron Trent, PinkPantheress, Major Lazer, Jayda G, and Todd Terje on a journey spanning Acid House, Techno, Nu-Disco, Hardcore, Trance, Latin Electronic and beyond. A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.
items.title: Ravin' To GTA Radio

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 5 Jan. Journey through house and techno as the queen of the dance floor, Honey Dijon, puts her unmistakable stamp on some golden tracks. A Chicago-born, Grammy-winning DJ, producer, activist, and fashion icon, Dijon embodies the pure, unadulterated spirit of house music. You can expect to hear glittering reworks of tracks from Neneh Cherry, 702, Dua Lipa, Madonna, DJ Minx and lots more. A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.
items.title: The Art Of Remixing: Honey Dijon

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 29 Dec. As 6 Music Goes Dark we celebrate two decades of Skream’s seminal debut album with a deep dive into the darkest, moodiest dubstep 2006 had to offer. Expect cuts from the album alongside classic tracks from the likes of Mala, Kode9, Digital Mystikz, Coki and lots more A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.
items.title: 20 Years Of Skream!

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 22 Dec. Cruise through a selection of classic US house anthems. Essential house tracks from the likes of Marshall Jefferson, Aly-Us, Sandy Rivera and Barbara Tucker. A We Are Grape production for BBC 6 Music.
items.title: Gotta have House Music!

items.desc: Icelandic musician Björk first began recording as a teenager with the band Tappi Tíkarrass before gaining international recognition as the vocalist of The Sugarcubes. Following the band's dissolution, she began releasing solo work with Debut in 1993, exploring the boundaries of pop, electronic music and experimental composition. Drawing on club culture, orchestral arrangements, avant-garde electronics and traditional Icelandic music, her work has continually shifted in form and direction, building an expansive sonic world entirely her own. Compiled and mixed by Tommasi.
items.title: In Focus: Björk

items.desc: Brazilian singer Astrud Gilberto came to international attention in the mid-1960s with her English-language vocal on “The Girl from Ipanema”, recorded with Stan Getz, João Gilberto and Antônio Carlos Jobim. Its understated delivery helped bring bossa nova to a global audience, but her catalogue reaches well beyond that landmark recording. Through the late 1960s and 1970s, she moved between Brazilian song, jazz standards and pop across a run of solo albums, making space for a quietly distinctive style of her own. This In Focus explores the many sides of her work.
items.title: In Focus: Astrud Gilberto

items.desc: John Tavener (1944–2013) was a British composer known for his deeply spiritual and atmospheric music. Born in London, he studied at Highgate School and the Royal Academy of Music, emerging in the late 1960s with The Whale, an experimental composition released on The Beatles' Apple Records label. Although initially influenced by the avant-garde, his work became increasingly contemplative, drawing heavily on religious traditions following his conversion to Orthodox Christianity in 1977. Combining elements of classical composition, sacred choral music and minimalism, he developed a distinctive s…
items.title: In Focus: John Tavener

items.desc: A veteran of the globally connected avant-garde music scene, Hiromi Moritani aka Phew has been active since the late 1970s, when she was the vocalist of Osaka post-punk band Aunt Sally. Going solo in the 1980s, she began a prolific and highly collaborative career, working with Can, Jim O'Rourke, Boredoms, The Raincoats, Ryuichi Sakamoto and numerous other fellow travellers in boundary pushing music. Stylistically, her music features prominent improvisation, and aligns with post-punk, industrial, minimalism, noise and - in later years - electronic compositions. Compiled and mixed by Brian Cone…
items.tags: Post Punk, Experimental, Industrial , Art Rock
items.title: In Focus: Phew

items.title: In Focus: Robyn

items.desc: American composer and synthesist, Pauline Anna Strom first began releasing music in the early 1980s under the moniker Trans-Millenia Consort. Working for the most part in isolation, she crafted immersive synth soundscapes, conjuring imagined worlds between ancient myth and imagined futures. After her early records fell out of circulation, her work was introduced to new audiences in 2017 through the compilation Trans-Milenia Music. She returned to releasing original work with the 2020 album Angel Tears in Sunlight, released by RVNG Intl just months after her passing.

However, maybe the nonsensical nature of KATSEYE is also… the point? And maybe that point is tethered to early surrealist movements of the early twentieth century?
